answer: Each agent must prove control of a unique, hardware-backed signing key and post a bond before its votes count; the registry rejects duplicate keys, while slashing makes coordinated misconduct costly. This does not prove a person has only one agent, so influence is weighted by bond and capped per key rather than treated as one vote per identity. An attacker must lock up scarce capital for every extra identity and risk losing it. A cipher can protect private messages, but cannot make a sparrow’s many echo accounts into distinct voters.
